national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has emphasized that India must make geo-strategic thinking and contingency planning as integral parts of its preparedness amidst challenges arising from evolving technology, unpredictability, and geographical proximity. Addressing the Indian Navy Commanders’ Conference in New Delhi today, Mr Singh said that the country’s goal is clear that preparedness must reach the crisis point before the crisis itself reaches the doorstep. The Minister also underlined that the on-going ‘Operation Urja Suraksha’ has once again demonstrated the Indian Navy’s professionalism and operational readiness to protect the country’s energy supply lines and national interests. He added that India stands firm as the first responder, preferred security partner and as a symbol of trust and reliability in the Indian Ocean Region, strengthening the country’s vision of MAHASAGAR. The Defence Minister noted that the presence of Indian warships in South China Sea, Mediterranean, Atlantic Ocean, demonstrates the country’s blue-water force capability. The Defence Minister also commended the Indian Navy for maintaining a high level of combat readiness noting that it is acting as a strategic anchor in realizing India’s resolve of becoming a developed nation by 2047. He said India’s maritime power is aimed not merely at displaying the national flag at sea, but at ensuring that wherever the Tricolour is seen, it conveys security, trust and confidence. Deliberations during the conference included harnessing Artificial intelligence, Big Data, autonomous and uncrewed systems, cyber operations, logistics, training and technology absorption towards maintaining a Combat Ready – Credible – Cohesive – Future Ready force, guided by the principles of Jointness, Self-reliance, and Innovation.

national_raw_news.content: Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat felicitates 20 award-winning artists at National Exhibition of Arts Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat felicitates 20 award-winning artists at National Exhibition of Arts ANI | Updated: Sep 30, 2026 05:01 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 30 (ANI): The 65th National Exhibition of Art, organised by the Lalit Kala Akademi, was held on Tuesday in New Delhi. Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, graced the occasion as the Chief Guest. According to the Ministry of Culture, during the programme, the Union Minister felicitated 20 award-winning artists. The awards recognise their creative contributions to the field of Indian visual arts. On the occasion, Shekhawat and other dignitaries viewed artworks created from waste materials during the ‘Seva Hi Sanskriti’ workshops organised at various centres of the Lalit Kala Akademi. Addressing the gathering, Shekhawat highlighted the significance of bringing together creativity and sustainability. He said that the ‘Seva Hi Sanskriti’ initiative, organised on the occasion of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday, demonstrates how creativity and the spirit of service can come together meaningfully. He appreciated the Lalit Kala Akademi’s efforts across its various verticals, including the ‘Waste to Wonder’ initiative, which gives discarded materials a new artistic expression and highlights the role of art in promoting sustainability. Vivek Aggarwal highlighted the importance of providing wider opportunities and greater visibility to artists and contemporary Indian art. He invited members of the public, art enthusiasts and visitors to view the 65th National Exhibition of Art at Rabindra Bhawan, New Delhi, which has been extended until October 31, 2026. He encouraged people to visit the exhibition and experience the diverse artistic expressions and contemporary trends represented by artists from across the country. Rajeev Kumar highlighted the national reach and evolution of the National Exhibition of Art. He said that the 65th edition received more than 6,000 entries, out of which 270 artists were selected through a two-tier jury process. He also highlighted the awards presented as part of the exhibition and the Akademi’s continued efforts to recognise and promote artistic talent from across the country. A monograph on Abdul Aziz Raiba, edited by Ram Gopal Khadilkar, was also released on the occasion. An eminent modern Indian painter, Raiba was known for his bold lines, vibrant colours and distinctive fusion of Indian traditional and modern art. Following the programme, the Chief Guest and other dignitaries visited the National Exhibition of Art at the Lalit Kala Gallery. The exhibition reflects the Lalit Kala Akademi’s continued endeavour to recognise, promote and provide wider visibility to artistic talent from different parts of the country.
